title: Hybrid stochastic router with kernel-aware prefill probes and rollback playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a hybrid stochastic routing layer that uses a fast prefill probe to compute a calibrated acceptance score combining predicted decode latency, kernel-fingerprint mismatch penalty, and decode-confidence (probe entropy). If the acceptance score exceeds a tunable threshold the request proceeds on an optimistic fast-path using a lighter-weight model/kernel variant; otherwise it falls back to the conservative full-path. The router must be kernel-selection-aware: model variants are annotated with a kernel fingerprint and estimated per-step cost so the acceptance function penalizes kernel mismatch or non-quantized execution paths.

Design highlights:
- Prefill probe: send a short prefill (1-2 tokens) through the serving runtime using the same KV/cache plumbing as production but with a capped work budget (time & memory). Collect: probe latency, probe log-prob distribution (entropy), attention memory footprint estimate, and kernel fingerprint.
- Acceptance function: calibrated logistic model: score = sigmoid(w1*latency_delta + w2*entropy + w3*kernel_mismatch_penalty + w4*model_priority_bias). We will expose the weights as runtime tunables and ship a default calibration trained on historical traces.
- Kernel fingerprinting: compile/loader will expose a short stable fingerprint (e.g., base64 of kernel selection table + quantization profile) per model variant. Router will include this in probe telemetry and apply mismatch penalties if the optimistic path would need a different kernel.
- Rollback mechanism: detect divergence via two signals: (1) decode-time anomaly (sudden token generation latency spike or acceptance confidence collapse) and (2) post-hoc semantic divergence measured by a lightweight edit-distance on token batches compared to safe-path stream. On rollback, the runtime will abort the optimistic stream and re-run the decode on the safe model variant from the last committed token. Streams are idempotent via sequence anchors so clients see a single monotonic token sequence.
- Safety floor: any request touching certain labels (e.g., `sensitive-env`, enterprise-SLA) bypasses optimistic routing and always routes to safe-path.

Acceptance metrics (to be emitted as router.* and kernel.* telemetry):
- router.accept_rate (per model, per route)
- router.false_accept_rate (cases where optimistic path later rolled back)
- router.rollback_rate (rollbacks per 10k requests)
- router.latency_delta_p50/p95 (safe-path vs optimistic)
- kernel.mismatch_rate (probe fingerprint != runtime path chosen)
- probe.latency_ms_p50/p95 and probe.confidence
- business metric: cost_per_100k_tokens_delta

Targets / SLOs (initial):
- target accept_rate ~ 60-75% on stable chat workloads
- false_accept_rate < 0.5% (goal) per 10k tokens
- rollback_rate < 0.1% per 10k requests for production tenant groups
- median latency improvement for served requests with optimistic routing >= 15%

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary: enabled for internal CI + non-customer workloads (1% traffic) for 2 weeks; monitor rotor metrics and PR curves.
2) Beta tenants: opt-in customers; monitor customer_impact label, false_accept_rate threshold triggers automatic disable.
3) Gradual ramp with automatic rollback based on rolling windows for rollback_rate and latency regressions.

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic suites: attention-heavy long-context prompts, adversarial high-entropy prompts, low-context bursts.
- A/B bench against existing optimistic prefills (use runtime perf harness).
- Chaos tests: GPU preemption, kernel eviction, and node drains to ensure graceful fallback and no token duplication.

Operational playbook (runbook snippets):
- If router.rollback_rate spikes > 0.5% for 5m: set router.global_threshold to conservative value and open SEV if customer impact > medium.
- If kernel.mismatch_rate climbs: re-evaluate compile stage and regenerate kernel hints; temporarily disable optimistic routing for affected model shard.

- Perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/router-acceptance

comments: 2026-02-21: Draft spec posted in Confluence. Early feedback from Maya: suggest adding an explicit kernel-fingerprint penalty term and expose as tunable. Action: update acceptance function to include kernel_mismatch_penalty. (Ava)

2026-03-05: Bench run with updated calibration shows false_accept_rate reduced to 0.9% and median latency improvement 22%. Still above false_accept target; plan: add kernel mismatch penalty + threshold annealing. (Liam)
2026-03-09: Security requested explicit list of labels that bypass optimistic routing. Created `safety_floor` label plan; assigned to Ava for review. (Maya)
2026-03-10: Updated acceptance logistic features and added kernel mismatch penalty; pushed PR updates and pinged Raj + Maya for review. Added unit tests for probe telemetry. (Liam)
